column4: Workflow change for chat-based runbook discovery — AWS announces general availability of 20 additional AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook recommendations as contextual action buttons on event notifications in AWS Chatbot.

Local change for multimodal embedding requests — Amazon Bedrock now offers multimodal support for Cohere Embed 3 Multilingual and Embed 3 English, foundation models that generate embeddings from both text and images.

Local change for Synthetics IPv6 probes — CloudWatch Synthetics now allows canaries running in a VPC to make outbound requests to IPv6 endpoints allowing monitoring of IPv6-only and dual stack enabled endpoints over IPv6.

Local change for case searches and list views — Amazon Connect Cases now allows agents and supervisors to filter cases in the agent workspace by custom field values, making it easier to narrow down search results and find relevant cases.

column3: contact center supervisors monitoring live calls
column4: Workflow change for contact center supervisors monitoring live calls — Amazon Connect Contact Lens now offers a new dashboard that lets you monitor real-time agent activity and take immediate actions such as listen-in to a contact, barge (take over) a contact, or change an agent state in a few clicks from a single interface.

Workflow change for agents handling consecutive calls — Amazon Connect now offers the ability to maintain an open communication channel between your agents and Amazon Connect, helping reduce the time it takes to establish a connection with a customer.
Local change for larger Flex instance workloads — AWS announces the general availability of two new larger sizes (12xlarge and 16xlarge) on Amazon EC2 Flex (C7i-flex, M7i-flex) instances.
Workflow change for ElastiCache quota management — Today, Amazon ElastiCache announces support for Service Quotas.

Workflow change for event source discovery — The Amazon EventBridge console now displays the source and detail type of all available AWS service events when you create a rule in the EventBridge console.
The managed collector replaces customer-operated telemetry agents in other accounts.
Workflow change for reconfiguring MSK connectors — Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports updating connector configuration of existing connectors.

Workflow change for Q Business users uploading images — Amazon Q Business, the most capable generative AI-powered assistant for finding information, gaining insight, and taking action at work, now offers capabilities to answer questions and extract insights from images uploaded in the chat.
Workflow change for onboarding Q Developer Pro users — The Amazon Q Developer Pro tier now offers automated email notifications for newly subscribed users.

Local change for new Redshift warehouse security — Amazon Redshift announces enhanced security defaults to help you adhere to best practices in data security and reduce the risk of potential misconfigurations.

Workflow change for geospatial H3 queries — Amazon Redshift extends support for Hexagonal Hierarchical Geospatial Indexing System, H3 for short, by adding two new H3 functions to Amazon Redshift’s previously announced H3 Indexing support in February 2024.
Local change for large S3 table catalogs — Amazon S3 Tables now support creating up to 10,000 tables in each S3 table bucket.
Local change for TypeScript clients in Lambda — AWS Amplify now enables developers to use the Amplify Data client within AWS Lambda functions.
Workflow change for users accessing multiple VPN profiles — Today, AWS announces the general availability of concurrent VPN connections for AWS Client VPN.
Workflow change for parallelizing CI test runs — You can now split your tests and run them across multiple, parallel-running compute environments.
Local change for DataSync Kerberos authentication — AWS DataSync now supports Kerberos authentication for self-managed file servers that use the Server Message Block (SMB) network protocol.
Fast Launch reduces Windows launch latency on the existing deployment path.

Workflow change for streaming video ad insertion — With AWS Elemental MediaTailor you can now bring your own pre-transcoded HLS and DASH packaged ads through VAST responses, enabling custom control over ad transcoding.

Local change for AWS Health IPv6 clients — AWS Health customers can now use Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) addresses, via our new dual-stack endpoints to view operational issues or planned lifecycle events for all accounts and resources in your organization.
Workflow change for multi-account console users — Today, AWS announces multi-session support, which enables AWS customers to access multiple AWS accounts simultaneously in the AWS Console.

Workflow change for AMI sellers using templates — AWS Marketplace now offers a self-service listing experience for sellers listing or managing Amazon Machine Image (AMI) products with CloudFormation templates (CFT).

Local change for Resource Explorer inventory — AWS Resource Explorer now supports 29 more resource types across all AWS commercial Regions from services including Amazon FSx, Amazon Route 53, and AWS Glue.

Workflow change for Step Functions API orchestration — AWS Step Functions expands its AWS SDK integrations with support for 36 additional AWS services including AWS End User Messaging and Amazon Q Apps, an Amazon Q Business capability.
Workflow change for WAF traffic analysis — AWS WAF’s console dashboard now includes richer visualizations that give you insights into the top sources of traffic.

Workflow change for Aurora PostgreSQL query diagnostics — Amazon CloudWatch Database Insights now collects the query execution plans of top SQL queries running on Aurora PostgreSQL instances, and stores them over time.

Workflow change for managed AWS notifications — Amazon Web Services (AWS) is announcing the general availability of AWS Managed Notifications, a new feature of AWS User Notifications that enhances how customers receive and manage AWS Health notifications.
Local change for Bedrock video generation — Luma AI's new video-generating AI foundation model (FM), Ray2, is now available in Amazon Bedrock.
Workflow change for QuickSight dashboard users — Dashboard Q&A by Amazon Q in QuickSight enables QuickSight Authors to add Data Q&A to their dashboards in one-click.

Workflow change for stateful GenAI sessions — Amazon Bedrock announces the preview launch of the Session Management APIs, a new capability that enables developers to simplify state and context management for generative AI (GenAI) applications built with popular open-source frameworks such as LangGraph and LlamaIndex.
Local change for case entry validation — Amazon Connect Cases now supports conditionally required fields to streamline case field population for agents and reduce data entry errors.

Workflow change for contact center evaluation delivery — Contact Lens now enables businesses to send automatic email notifications to agents when their contacts are evaluated, so they can review the evaluations and improve their performance.

Workflow change for contact center schedule drafting — Amazon Connect now includes agent time-off requests in draft schedules, making it easier for you to view why an agent was not scheduled on a particular day or part of the day.

Workflow change for CloudShell database access — Starting today, you can connect to your Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) clusters with a single click through AWS CloudShell directly from the AWS Management Console.

column3: SQL Server recovery from VSS snapshots
column4: Workflow change for SQL Server recovery from VSS snapshots — Amazon EC2 now supports automated recovery of Microsoft SQL Server databases from Volume Shadow Copy Services (VSS) based EBS snapshots.
Local change for time-bounded AMI copies — Amazon EC2 announces the general availability of Time-based Copy for Amazon Machine Images (AMIs).

Workflow change for ECS service ARN migration — You can now update your existing Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that use a short Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to use a long ARN without needing to re-create the service.
Local change for FSx API clients — Amazon FSx now offers customers the option to use Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) while accessing the Amazon FSx Service APIs .
Local change for large time-series search collections — We are excited to announce that Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports workloads up to 100TB of data for time-series collections.

Workflow change for Q Business query routing — Amazon Q Business, the generative AI-powered assistant for finding information, gaining insight, and taking action at work, introduced an intelligent orchestration feature that simplifies conversational experience by understanding user queries, and automatically directing the queries to the right data sources and plugins to generate relevant responses.
Local change for Java application upgrades — Amazon Q Developer transformation capabilities that allow customers to upgrade Java applications using Maven to Java 21 are now available.
Local change for Redshift Serverless subnet planning — Amazon Redshift Serverless announces reduction in IP Address Requirements to 3 per Subnet.

Workflow change for SSR applications accessing AWS resources — We're excited to announce the launch of IAM compute roles for AWS Amplify Hosting, enabling secure connections to other AWS resources from server-side rendered applications.
Local change for GraphQL response caching — AWS AppSync GraphQL now offers operation-level caching, a new feature that allows customers to cache entire GraphQL query operation responses.

Workflow change for Batch workloads on EKS — AWS Batch on EKS now supports configurable Kubernetes namespaces, Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs), subPath to Kubernetes pod container volumes, and Kubernetes pod annotations.
Workflow change for Transfer Family infrastructure deployment — You can now use AWS CloudFormation templates to create and manage your AWS Transfer Family web apps.
Build jobs can run on CodeBuild ephemeral hosts instead of customer-operated runner hosts.

Workflow change for CodePipeline monitoring — AWS CodePipeline now provides Amazon CloudWatch metrics integration for V2 pipelines, enabling you to monitor both pipeline-level and account-level metrics directly in your AWS account.
The native EC2 action removes separately managed CodeDeploy resources and AppSpec configuration.
Local change for After Effects rendering jobs — AWS Deadline Cloud now includes support for Adobe After Effects in its Service-Managed Fleets.

Local change for behavioral health notes — AWS HealthScribe is a generative AI-powered service that automatically generates summarized clinical notes and transcripts from patient-clinician conversations.

Workflow change for IoT certificate operations — Today, AWS IoT Device Defender introduced two features to simplify IoT certificate lifecycle management - a new audit check for certificate age and enhancements to the existing device certificate expiring audit check.
Workflow change for firewall policy administration — AWS Network Firewall now provides enhanced console capabilities that improve rule management and policy configuration workflows.

Workflow change for EKS secrets access — Today, AWS Secrets Manager announces that AWS Secrets and Configuration Provider (ASCP) now integrates with Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Pod Identity.
Workflow change for DocumentDB developers using VS Code — AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code (VSCode) now includes Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility).
Workflow change for WAF quota requests — AWS WAF enhances Service Quotas capabilities, enabling organizations to proactively monitor and manage quotas for their cloud deployments.

Local change for .NET runtime monitoring — Today, AWS is announcing the general availability of runtime metrics for .NET applications in Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals, an OpenTelemetry (OTel)-compatible application performance monitoring (APM) feature in CloudWatch.

Workflow change for RDS MySQL and MariaDB diagnostics — Amazon CloudWatch Database Insights expands the availability of its on-demand analysis experience to the RDS for MySQL and RDS for MariaDB database engines.

column3: Word and Outlook users querying business data
column4: Workflow change for Word and Outlook users querying business data — Today, AWS announces the general availability of the Amazon Q Business integrations for Microsoft 365 for Word and Outlook.
Mail Manager Archives can receive outbound SES messages directly, changing the archive delivery path.
Workflow change for testing zonal autoshift recovery — AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) now supports a recovery action for Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal autoshift.

Workflow change for multimodal document extraction — Today, we are announcing the general availability of Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA), a feature of Amazon Bedrock that enables developers to automate the generation of valuable insights from unstructured multimodal content such as documents, images, video, and audio to build GenAI-based applications.
A managed knowledge base builds and stores the embedding and entity graph in Neptune Analytics.
Bedrock orchestrates a network of specialized agents through a supervisor.
A single App Monitor can collect telemetry across domains that previously required multiple monitors.

Workflow change for contact center evaluation acknowledgment — You can now capture and review agent acknowledgements of performance evaluations within Contact Lens, ensuring that agents have reviewed evaluation feedback and understand performance expectations.

Workflow change for dynamic evaluation forms — Contact Lens now enables you to create dynamic evaluation forms that automatically show or hide questions based on responses to previous questions, tailoring each evaluation to specific customer interaction scenarios.
Firehose delivers stream records directly into a table without a custom multi-step delivery pipeline.
An interface endpoint provides a private route that removes the internet gateway dependency.
Local change for large EC2 I8g workloads — AWS announces the general availability of one new larger sizes (48xlarge) on Amazon EC2 I8g instances in US East(N.

Workflow change for EKS cluster upgrades — Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) announced a new control to prevent accidental cluster upgrades when issues are already detected that may impact application compatibility with the next Kubernetes version.

Workflow change for EMR job credentials — Today, Amazon EMR on EKS announces support for Amazon EKS Pod Identity , simplifying the setup of IAM permissions required by EMR on EKS jobs to access other AWS resources.
Interface endpoints replace the public route through a gateway or proxy.
Local change for minimal container vulnerability scans — Today, we are excited to announce support for scratch, distroless (Debian/Ubuntu based), and Chainguard image scanning with Amazon Inspector.
Local change for Kinesis IPv6 consumers — Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now allows customers to make API requests over Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6).
Local change for Nova tool selection — Amazon Nova now supports expanded Tool Choice parameter options in the Converse API , enhancing developers' control over model interactions with tools.

Workflow change for command-line development — Today, Amazon Q Developer announced an enhanced CLI agent within the Amazon Q command line interface (CLI) that allows you to have more dynamic conversations.
Local change for PostgreSQL TLS configuration — Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL now supports modifying the ssl_ciphers parameter.
Local change for Redshift Serverless update timing — Amazon Redshift Serverless is now available on two different release cycles - Current Track and Trailing Track.
Workflow change for S3 Access Grants users — Amazon S3 Access Grants now authenticate based on the union of both Identity Provider (IdP) and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions.
Batchwise rolling updates replace blue/green duplicate fleets for supported endpoints.

Workflow change for inbound email security — Today, Amazon SES announces the availability of the Vade Add On for Mail Manager, a sophisticated content filter that enhances email security for both incoming and outgoing messages.
Workflow change for Terraform-managed computing clusters — Today, we are announcing Terraform support for AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS).

Workflow change for WebSocket event publishers — AppSync Events adds publishing over WebSocket for real-time pub/sub. AWS AppSync Events is a fully managed service that allows developers to create secure and performant WebSocket APIs.
Workflow change for protecting hosted Amplify applications — Today, we are announcing the general availability of our Web Application Firewall Protection for AWS Amplify Hosting .

Local change for large Client VPN route tables — Today, AWS announces increased quotas for AWS Client VPN, expanding routes per target network association to 100 and authorization rules per endpoint to 200.

column3: CodeBuild jobs requiring direct host access
column4: Builds can execute directly on the host instead of inside a container.

Workflow change for CodePipeline quality gates — AWS CodePipeline V2 type pipeline introduces CodeBuild rule and Commands rule that customers can use in their stage level condition to gate a pipeline execution.

Local change for Db2 migration conversions — AWS DMS Schema Conversion now supports conversions from IBM Db2 for z/OS to Amazon RDS for Db2. AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) Schema Conversion is a fully managed feature of DMS that automatically assesses and converts database schemas to formats compatible with AWS target database services.
Local change for mobile console administration — Today, AWS announced support for 24 additional AWS services in the AWS Console Mobile App.

Local change for IAM IPv6 callers — AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) announces a new dual-stack public endpoint, enabling customers to connect to IAM over the public internet using IPv6, IPv4, or dual-stack clients.
Workflow change for registering payment cards in Japan — AWS has enabled Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for card registration in Japan to enhance payment security.

column3: Cloud WAN management from private networks
column4: A PrivateLink endpoint provides a private control-plane path without traversing the public internet.

Local change for Resource Access Manager IPv6 clients — AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) customers can now use Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) addresses, via our new dual-stack endpoints to create and manage RAM resource shares in your accounts.

column3: Step Functions developers in VS Code
column4: Workflow change for Step Functions developers in VS Code — AWS Step Functions Workflow Studio is now available in the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code, enabling you to visually create, edit, and debug state machine workflows directly in your local development environment.
The announcement describes eligibility, certification or guidance without documenting a change in customer workflow. AWS Verified Access achieves FedRAMP High and Moderate authorization.
Local change for WAF URI matching — AWS WAF now supports URI fragment field matching, enabling customers to match against the URI fragment and along with the already supported URI path .

Workflow change for Bottlerocket bootstrap setup — Today, AWS has announced that Bottlerocket, the Linux-based operating system purpose-built for containers, now provides a default bootstrap container image that simplifies system setup tasks, eliminating the need for most customers to maintain their own container images for initial configuration.
Local change for Bedrock DeepSeek inference — DeepSeek-R1 is now available as a fully managed, serverless model in Amazon Bedrock.

Local change for quantum hardware selection — Amazon Braket, the quantum computing service from AWS, now offers IonQ's latest 36-qubit Forte Enterprise quantum processing unit (QPU) in the US East (N.

Workflow change for fine-tuning Llama models — Amazon Bedrock now supports fine-tuning for Meta’s Llama 3.2 models (1B, 3B, 11B, and 90B), enabling businesses to customize these generative AI models with their own data.
Workflow change for Wickr administrators — AWS Wickr is excited to announce a redesigned admin experience that's now fully integrated with the AWS Management Console.

Workflow change for collaborative Spark processing — Today, AWS announces the general availability of PySpark in AWS Clean Rooms, enabling companies and their partners to run sophisticated analytics across large datasets using PySpark, the Python API for Apache Spark .

Workflow change for Salesforce contact center agents — Salesforce Contact Center with Amazon Connect , now generally available, is a groundbreaking offering that integrates native digital and voice capabilities into Salesforce Service Cloud, delivering a unified and streamlined experience for agents.
Local change for SLO exclusions — Customers can now set exclusion time windows to avoid affecting a service's reliability score during planned downtime.

Workflow change for multimodal document extraction — Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) now supports modality enablement, modality routing by file type, extraction of embedded hyperlinks when processing documents in Standard Output, and an increased overall document page limit of 3,000 pages.

Workflow change for Bedrock inference routing — Amazon Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing routes prompts to different foundation models within a model family, helping you optimize for quality of responses and cost.

Local change for model evaluation — Amazon Bedrock Evaluations allows you to evaluate foundation models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, whether hosted on Amazon Bedrock or multicloud and on-prem deployments.

Local change for ROSA monitoring — Amazon CloudWatch agent support for Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) enables monitoring of applications and infrastructure using familiar CloudWatch tools such as Container Insights and Application Signals.

Local change for machine authorization flows — Amazon Cognito now allows you to include additional contextual information in the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow for M2M access token requests, enhancing your control over machine-based interactions.

Workflow change for agent workspace integrations — The Amazon Connect agent workspace now supports additional capabilities for third-party applications including the ability make outbound calls, accept, transfer, and clear contacts, and update agent status.
Workflow change for tracking case SLAs — Amazon Connect Cases now provides capabilities to help contact centers track and meet service level agreements (SLAs) on cases.

Local change for voice contact flows — Amazon Connect now provides the ability to dynamically set the text-to-speech (TTS) voices, language, or speaking styles used in voice bots and interactive voice response (IVR).
Local change for snapshot permissions — Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) now supports additional resource-level permissions for copying EBS snapshots .
Local change for EC2 bare metal — Today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announces the launch of two new EC2 I7ie bare metal instances.
Local change for hybrid node OS selection — Today, AWS announced Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes support for Bottlerocket, the Linux-based operating system purpose-built for containers.

Workflow change for ONTAP ransomware detection — Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP , a service that provides fully managed shared storage built on NetApp’s popular ONTAP file system, now supports ONTAP Autonomous Ransomware Protection (ARP).
Local change for Lex intent elicitation — Amazon Lex now allows you to disable automatic intent switching during slot elicitation using request attributes.

Workflow change for custom image generation — Amazon Nova Canvas now supports fine-tuning through Amazon Bedrock, enabling customers to adapt the model to their unique datasets and brand characteristics.
One speech-to-speech model combines speech understanding and generation in the conversational pipeline.

Workflow change for CLI agent tool integration — Today, Amazon Q Developer announced support for Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Amazon Q Developer Command Line Interface (CLI), enabling developers to leverage tools and prompts to support richer contextual, development workflows.
Workflow change for QuickSight publishing — Amazon QuickSight launches dashboard versioning and the ability to publish any analysis to replace any dashboard to improve author productivity.
Local change for Oracle instance sizing — Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports R6id and M6id instances.

Workflow change for managing private hosted zones — Today, AWS announced support for VPC endpoints in Amazon Route 53 Profiles, allowing you to create, manage, and share private hosted zones (PHZs) for interface VPC endpoints across multiple VPCs and AWS accounts within your organization.

Local change for catalog identifier search — Amazon SageMaker Catalog, part of the next generation of Amazon SageMaker, now supports enhanced search capabilities with exact-match and partial-match functionality for technical identifiers such as column and table names.

Workflow change for restoring Studio application access — We are excited to announce that Amazon SageMaker Studio now supports recovery mode, enabling users to regain access to their JupyterLab and Code Editor applications when configuration issues prevent normal startup.
Workflow change for email attachments — Today, Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) launched support for adding attachments to emails when sending via SES simple sending v2 APIs.

Local change for SNS IPv6 callers — Amazon SNS now supports Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) for API requests enabling you to communicate with Amazon SNS using Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6), Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4), or dual stack clients using public endpoints.

Local change for VPC Lattice API clients — Amazon VPC Lattice introduces dual stack support for management API, enabling you to connect using Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6), Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4), or dual stack clients.

Workflow change for autoscaled ingestion pipelines — Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion now supports enhanced autoscaling capabilities, allowing pipelines to scale dynamically based on additional parameters, including Amazon SQS queue size, persistent buffer lag, and the number of incoming HTTP connections.
Workflow change for development data seeding — AWS Amplify now supports seeding data across Amazon Cognito, AWS AppSync, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3.
The announcement describes eligibility, certification or guidance without documenting a change in customer workflow. AWS Application Migration Service authorized for DoD Impact Level 4 and 5.

column3: ECS Exec and FireLens on Batch
column4: Local change for ECS Exec and FireLens on Batch — AWS Batch now supports Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) Exec and AWS FireLens log router for AWS Batch on Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate.

Workflow change for Spark SQL collaboration rules — With today’s launch, AWS Clean Rooms provides additional privacy-enhancing controls to support aggregation and list analysis rules using the Spark analytics engine.
Workflow change for debugging builds — AWS CodeBuild now supports enhanced debugging experience through secure and isolated sandbox environments.

Local change for Lightsail mobile management — AWS customers can now access Amazon Lightsail from within the AWS Console Mobile App to monitor and manage Lightsail instances, containers, databases, network, storage, snapshots, domains and DNS while on the go.
Local change for Beanstalk security groups — AWS Elastic Beanstalk now gives customers the option to use default security groups or their own custom security groups when deploying applications.
Workflow change for SMS fraud prevention — Today, AWS End User Messaging introduces new features to help developers combat artificially inflated traffic (AIT), also known as SMS pumping.
Workflow change for bioinformatics workflows — AWS HealthOmics now supports workflow versioning, enabling customers to manage multiple versions of their bioinformatics workflows efficiently.

Workflow change for mainframe runtime management — We are excited to announce that AWS Mainframe Modernization service is now available with greater control of managed runtime environments that run modernized mainframe applications.

Local change for resource inventories — AWS Resource Explorer now supports 32 more resource types across all AWS commercial Regions from services including Amazon API Gateway, AWS CloudTrail, and Amazon CloudFront.
Local change for private REST domains — AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) now supports custom domain names for private REST APIs feature of Amazon API Gateway .

Local change for regional token requests — AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) now automatically serves all requests to the global endpoint (sts.amazonaws.com) in the same AWS Region as your deployed workloads, enhancing resiliency and performance.
Workflow change for remote SFTP file operations — AWS Transfer Family now enables you to delete, rename, or move files on remote SFTP servers using SFTP connectors.

Workflow change for image parameter references — EC2 Image Builder now integrates with Systems Manager Parameter Store , offering customers a streamlined approach for referencing SSM parameters in their image recipes, components, and distribution configurations.
Workflow change for OpenSearch ingestion design — Today, we're announcing a new visual user interface for creating and editing Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion pipelines on the AWS console.

Local change for gateway load balancer capacity — Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) now supports Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation that allows you to proactively set a minimum bandwidth capacity for your load balancer, complementing its existing ability to auto-scale based on your traffic pattern.

Local change for governance controls — Today, AWS announces that AWS Control Tower supports an additional 223 managed Config rules in Control Catalog for various use cases such as security, cost, durability, and operations.

Workflow change for multitenant content delivery — Today, AWS announces CloudFront SaaS Manager, a new Amazon CloudFront feature designed to efficiently manage content delivery across multiple websites for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) providers, web development platforms, and companies with multiple brands/websites.
PrivateLink connects the application VPC to a Mail Manager ingress endpoint before delivery to external recipients.
Workflow change for resizing Memcached nodes — Today, Amazon ElastiCache introduces the ability to perform vertical scaling on self-designed Memcached caches on ElastiCache.

Local change for Aurora regional switchovers — Amazon Aurora for MySQL and Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL now offer faster Global Database cross-Region switchover, reducing recovery time for read/write operations to typically under 30 seconds and enhancing availability for applications operating at a global scale.

Workflow change for custom video analysis — Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) now supports video blueprints so you can generate tailored, accurate insights in a consistent format for your multimedia analysis applications.

Workflow change for distilling Bedrock models — Model Distillation is the process of transferring knowledge from a more capable model (teacher) to a less capable one (student) with the goal to make the faster and cost-efficient student model as performant as the teacher for a specific use-case.

Local change for browser performance tracking — Today, CloudWatch RUM, a real-time monitoring service that visualizes and analyzes user interactions with web applications, announces support for Interaction to Next Paint (INP) web vital monitoring.
Local change for Lambda log delivery — Today, Amazon CloudWatch launched volume tiered pricing for AWS Lambda logs and support for additional delivery destinations.

Workflow change for agent adherence monitoring — Amazon Connect Contact Lens now include a pre-configured agent adherence widget which supports filtering and sorting on agent adherence metrics, making day-to-day adherence management more efficient for supervisors.

Workflow change for post-contact processing — Amazon Connect now publishes a new contact completion event in the Contact Event Stream (via Amazon EventBridge), delivering real-time insights into when a contact has fully concluded, including the completion of any after-contact work (ACW).
Local change for GPU compute workloads — Today, AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) P6-B200 instances, accelerated by NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

Workflow change for ECS rollback — Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) announced a new feature that allows you to easily rollback your Amazon ECS service to a previous safe state if a deployment fails.
Workflow change for EKS hybrid configuration — Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Services (Amazon EKS) announced the general availability of configuration insights for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes.

Local change for FlexCache writeback — Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, a service that provides fully managed shared storage built on NetApp’s popular ONTAP file system, now supports write-back mode for ONTAP FlexCache volumes.

Workflow change for IVS participant replication — Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Real-Time Streaming now supports participant replication, allowing you to copy a participant from one IVS stage to another.
Local change for Prometheus range queries — Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now supports queries with time ranges up to 95 days, an increase from the previous 32-day limit.

Workflow change for Airflow environment updates — Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) now provides the option to update environments without interrupting running tasks on supported Apache Airflow versions (v2.4.3 or later).

Local change for OpenSearch script execution — Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports Script Plugins that allow you to add new scripting languages or custom scripting functionality to OpenSearch for operations like scoring, sorting, and field value transformations during search or indexing.
Workflow change for GitHub software development — Today, AWS announces the preview of the Amazon Q Developer integration in GitHub.
Workflow change for database lifecycle planning — Amazon RDS announces a new capability that helps you view engine lifecycle support dates for your databases.

Local change for notebook code suggestions — Today, AWS announces significant enhancements to Amazon Q Developer in Amazon SageMaker AI Jupyter Lab, introducing customization of code suggestions based on private code repositories and the ability to include entire workspace context for improved code assistance.

Workflow change for S3 Tables governance — Amazon SageMaker Catalog integrates with Amazon S3 Tables, making it easy to discover, share, and govern S3 Tables for users to access and query the data with all Apache Iceberg–compatible tools and engines.
The Lakehouse can query Oracle, DocumentDB or SQL Server directly over the new connections.
Local change for SES outbound IPv6 callers — Today, Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) launched support for connecting to SES outbound sending endpoints over IPv6.
Workflow change for VPC audit events — Amazon VPC has enhanced CloudTrail logging to include VPC resources created by default during a VPC creation.

Local change for Bedrock Claude inference — The next generation of Anthropic's Claude models, Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 , are now available in Amazon Bedrock, representing significant advancements in AI capabilities.

Local change for Aurora DSQL backups — AWS Backup now provides fully managed data protection capabilities for Amazon Aurora DSQL , a serverless distributed SQL database for always available applications.

Workflow change for synthetic test updates — Today, CloudWatch Synthetics, which allows monitoring of customer workflows on websites through periodically running custom code scripts, announces two new features: canary safe updates and automatic retries for failing canaries.

Local change for EC2 deployment parameters — AWS CodePipeline now supports Deploy Spec file configurations in the EC2 Deploy action, enabling you to specify deployment parameters directly in your source repository.
Workflow change for governance status reporting — AWS Control Tower customers can now programmatically view statuses for their governed accounts via baseline APIs.
Workflow change for monthly cost comparisons — AWS announces Cost Comparison, a new AWS Cost Explorer capability that helps customers understand cost changes between two months.
Workflow change for render fleet configuration — AWS Deadline Cloud now supports specifying a configuration script on both Linux and Windows service-managed fleets.
Local change for Glue Studio file IO — Today, AWS Glue Studio announces support for additional compressed file types, Excel files (as source), and XML and Tableau's Hyper files (as target).
Workflow change for series-level metadata retrieval — Today, AWS HealthImaging announces support for retrieving the metadata for all DICOM instances in a series via a single API action.
Local change for listing SaaS products — AWS Marketplace now supports software as a service (SaaS) products deployed on AWS, on other cloud infrastructures, and on-premises.

Local change for Organizations IPv6 callers — AWS Organizations customers can now use Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) addresses, via our new dual-stack endpoints to connect to AWS Organizations over the public internet using IPv6, IPv4, or dual-stack clients.
Workflow change for secret cost allocation — AWS Secrets Manager now enables customers to allocate and track cost for their secret usage.

Local change for SFTP key negotiation — AWS Transfer Family now supports ML- KEM (FIPS-203), a post-quantum algorithm standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), for SFTP file transfers.

Workflow change for Unified Studio coding — Today, AWS announces two complementary capabilities in the next generation of Amazon SageMaker that enhance the development experience for analytics, machine learning (ML), and GenAI teams: Code Editor and Multiple Spaces support.

Workflow change for cloud database development — Today, Amazon DynamoDB announces the general availability of DynamoDB local on AWS CloudShell, a browser-based, pre-authenticated shell that you can launch directly from the AWS Management Console.
Local change for EC2 IPv6 addressing — EC2 Public DNS names can now resolve to IPv6 Global Unicast Address (AAAA record) associated with your EC2 instances and Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI).
Local change for automounting S3 buckets — Mountpoint for Amazon S3 now lets you automatically mount an S3 bucket when your Amazon EC2 instance starts up.
Workflow change for console troubleshooting — Today, we’re announcing new and improved agentic Amazon Q Developer experience in the AWS Management Console, Microsoft Teams, and Slack.
Local change for importing Qwen weights — Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import now supports Qwen models.

Local change for log processing — Amazon CloudWatch pipelines now includes three new processors that parse and enrich log data as it's ingested: an Amazon RDS log parser, an XML parser and a GeoIP enrichment processor.

Workflow change for major database upgrades — Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) now supports in-place major version upgrades (MVU) directly from engine versions 3.6 and 4.0 to version 8.0.

Workflow change for domain-joined Windows deployments — AWS Elastic Beanstalk now automatically joins the Windows Server instances in your environment to an Active Directory domain that you manage with AWS Directory Service.
Local change for GameLift capacity selection — Amazon GameLift Servers now supports 21 additional Amazon EC2 instance types for managed EC2 fleets and managed container fleets.
Workflow change for generating IAM policies — IAM Policy Autopilot can now generate baseline IAM policies directly from a Terraform plan file.

Workflow change for ad monetization analysis — AWS Elemental MediaTailor now includes an analytics dashboard built directly into the AWS Management Console, giving publishers a global and multi-region view of ad monetization and streaming performance — with the ability to compare across regions and drill into individual playback configurations.
Nested virtualization eliminates the separate hardware or workaround environments needed for hypervisor-dependent tools.
Local change for OpenSearch UI network policy — Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports network access controls for OpenSearch UI applications.

Local change for streaming Redshift capacity — Amazon Redshift , starting with patch P203 , supports concurrency scaling for refreshes of Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (KDS)-connected streaming materialized views (MVs).

Workflow change for coordinating regional failovers — Today, we are launching the Amazon RDS Switchover Read Replica execution block in ARC Region switch , which automates recovery orchestration for Amazon RDS databases running Oracle Data Guard in multi-Region workloads.
Workflow change for workforce adherence — Amazon Connect Customer now gives supervisors visibility into how well agents followed their schedules with historical agent adherence metrics on dashboards.

Local change for feature store writes — Amazon SageMaker Feature Store now supports individual feature updates to lower write latency. Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a fully managed capability that makes it easy to compute, store, and retrieve features for training and deploying AI models.
A FIPS interface endpoint replaces the formerly public-only encrypted service path.

Workflow change for installing workload credentials — Today, AWS Secrets Manager announces one-click installation for the AWS Workload Credentials Provider (AWCP) on Amazon Linux and Windows, reducing setup from a multi-step build-from-source process to a single command.
Workflow change for new AWS builders — Builders can now sign up for a new simplified experience that makes it faster to turn ideas into running code on AWS.
Local change for execution log delivery — Amazon API Gateway now supports configurable delivery destinations and larger log events for REST API execution logs.
A hosted consent portal replaces customer-operated callback infrastructure.

Workflow change for refreshing RAG data — AWS announces automatic sync scheduling for Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, a fully managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) service that handles data ingestion, storage optimization, and advanced retrieval without requiring you to manage vector databases or data pipelines.
Native connectors replace custom pipelines for crawling and incremental synchronization.
Local change for per-agent task capacity — Amazon Connect Customer now gives contact center managers the ability to set specific capacity limits for different kinds of work.
Workflow change for employee shift preferences — Amazon Connect Customer now enables agents to bid on preferred shifts, giving them more control over their work schedules.

Local change for DocumentDB aggregation queries — Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) now supports retryable writes, 5 new aggregation stages, and change stream enhancements starting from minor version 8.0.2.

Workflow change for ECS daemon rollout monitoring — Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now provides a consolidated deployment view for Amazon ECS Managed Daemons, giving you a single place to see how far a deployment has progressed, what is failing, and what could stop it.

Local change for ARM container workloads — Amazon Elastic Container Service Express Mode now supports specifying ARM64 as the CPU architecture for your service, making it easy to deploy ARM-based container images on AWS Graviton-powered compute and benefit from up to 40% better price-performance compared to x86-based instances.
Public endpoints remove the need for a VPN, bastion host or SSH tunnel to reach the cache.
Workflow change for stream API validation — Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports a dry run feature to check whether an API request would succeed without executing the operation.

Workflow change for Vercel search application development — You can now build full-stack search and AI applications in minutes using Amazon OpenSearch Serverless on v0 by Vercel, an AI-powered platform that transforms your ideas into production-ready web applications.

Workflow change for always-on research agents — Today, Amazon Quick offers new capabilities that make it easier to organize your work, govern it across an organization, and trust the answers it produces.
Developer Edition maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover.

Local change for Iceberg data typing — Amazon S3 Tables add support for geometry, geography, unknown, and nanosecond timestamp data types, along with column default values, as defined in the Apache Iceberg Version 3 (V3) specification.

Workflow change for signing outgoing email — Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) now supports Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) signing, giving you a way to help recipients verify your emails are authentic.

Local change for encrypted speech resources — Amazon Transcribe now lets you encrypt your custom vocabularies, custom vocabulary filters, and custom language models at rest with a customer-managed AWS KMS key that you own and control.

Local change for virtual desktop GPU workloads — Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports Graphics G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and Intel Xeon 6 processors.

Local change for RDS instance sizing — Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB now support M8a database instances powered by 5th generation AMD EPYC processors, expanding the choice available for your database workloads.
Workflow change for air-gapped ONTAP backups — AWS Backup logically air-gapped vault now supports Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

Workflow change for billing context lookup — AWS Billing and Cost Management now offers the ListBillingViewSegments API, which returns the billing context of your account over a time period you specify.

Workflow change for toolkit skill management — Today, AWS expanded the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) commands for the Agent Toolkit for AWS with two new capabilities that make it easier to keep agent skills up to date.

Workflow change for auditing CloudTrail coverage — AWS CloudTrail introduces Event Coverage, a new console experience that gives customers visibility into their data plane operations coverage at the account and organization level.
Workflow change for cross-account transfer networking — AWS DataSync now supports shared Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs).

Workflow change for ad response handling — AWS Elemental MediaTailor now supports two additional lifecycle hooks for monetization functions: post ad decision server (ADS) response, and pre manifest insertion.

Local change for 10DLC number procurement — AWS End User Messaging now lets you choose the area code when you request a ten digit long code (10DLC) phone number for sending SMS to recipients in the United States.

Local change for GWLB failure recovery — A WS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) now supports sending TCP Reset (RST) packets when a target becomes unhealthy, is deregistered, or when a flow's idle timeout expires.

Local change for long Lambda functions — AWS Lambda now supports a 90-minute function timeout for asynchronous and event source mapping (ESM) invocations on Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) , a 6x increase from the previous 15-minute limit.
Local change for Graviton-based Lambda compute — AWS Lambda now supports AWS Graviton5-powered C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd instances on Lambda Managed Instances .

Workflow change for agent-managed Lambda development — Today, AWS Model Context Protocol Server (AWS MCP Server) added a serverless capability so that coding agents such as Claude Code and Kiro can efficiently diagnose issues with your Lambda functions.
Workflow change for HPC scaling diagnostics — AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) now supports scaling logs, which record how AWS PCS scales the compute node groups in your cluster.
A VPC endpoint serves the discovery document and verification keys without public internet access.

Workflow change for CLI-based .NET modernization — Today, AWS announced the general availability of an AWS-managed transformation for .NET modernization in AWS Transform custom that you can trigger with a single one-line CLI command.
Local change for frontier model inference — Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available on AWS and brings Anthropic's most capable frontier model to all customers.

Workflow change for CloudFront subscriptions — Starting today, customers can subscribe and manage flat-rate pricing plans programmatically using the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, CloudFormation, CDK, or the PricingPlanManager API.

Workflow change for estimating log query cost — Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights now lets you estimate the volume of log data, in bytes, that a query would scan over your selected log groups and time range - without running the query.

Local change for tagged metric permissions — Amazon Connect Customer now supports tag-based access control for custom metrics, so you can govern which users and roles can view, create, or modify each custom metric.
Workflow change for tracking account transfers — AWS DataSync now provides a monitoring dashboard in the DataSync console that gives you visibility into your data transfers across your account.
Workflow change for cross-account volume copies — Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Volume Clones now supports copying EBS volumes across AWS accounts with re-encryption.
Local change for burstable EC2 workloads — AWS is announcing the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances.
Local change for Graviton disaster recovery — AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) now supports disaster recovery for AWS Graviton-based (arm64) source servers.
Workflow change for interactive Spark analysis — Amazon EMR on EKS now supports interactive Apache Spark sessions with Spark Connect.
Workflow change for generating analysis sheets — Amazon Quick now expands Generate Analysis with two new ways to create dashboards faster.
Workflow change for managing replicated metadata — AWS Glue zero-ETL integrations now detect table property conflicts and track integration ownership.
Interface endpoints remove internet gateways, NAT and public IPs from video ingest and playback paths.
Workflow change for live contact center coordination — Amazon Connect Customer announces the general availability of Live Sync and Touchpoint.
Workflow change for locking video pipelines — AWS Elemental MediaLive now supports Video Aligned Locking, a new feature to synchronize video pipelines without requiring timecode from the source.
Local change for Kimi model inference — Amazon Bedrock continues to expand its open weight model portfolio with the same security and governance that customers rely on.
Local change for Bedrock GPT inference — Today, AWS announces the general availability of GPT-6.1 Sol from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock.
Local change for GPT-6 applications — Today, AWS announces the general availability of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock.

Workflow change for guided dashboard navigation — Amazon Quick now supports the hierarchy filter, a single control that lets readers drill through related dimensions such as Region, Country, and City.

Workflow change for secure Redshift log access — Amazon Redshift now makes it easier to troubleshoot and audit queries on data protected by federated permissions with fine-grained access control (FGAC).
Customers monitoring sign-in events must collect CloudTrail events in three regions.

Local change for filtered vector queries — Amazon S3 Vectors now supports pre-filtering, which evaluates metadata filters before running similarity search, returning up to 5x more of the matching vectors when your filter is selective.

Workflow change for remote catalog access — Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports two new connection capabilities: (1) Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC) connections for external Apache Iceberg catalogs, and (2) IAM authentication for Amazon DocumentDB.
Local change for multicloud AI inventory — AWS Security Hub AI Inventory now supports discovering and cataloging AI assets running on self-hosted instances in Microsoft Azure.
FIPS interface endpoints replace public-only transit for file shares and service management.
Workflow change for InfluxDB processing plugins — Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB now lets you run your own custom Python plugins on the managed versions of InfluxDB 3 Core and Enterprise editions.
Workflow change for bulk file downloads — AWS Transfer Family now lets web app users download multiple files and folders at once.

Workflow change for resilient model invocation — Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway now supports the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs on its inference endpoint, along with model fallback routing for inference traffic.

Workflow change for agentic contact workflows — Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to use flow modules as data requests in agentic CX designer, so you can build and apply reusable logic across your customer experience flows.
Local change for model response inspection — Amazon Bedrock now supports the reasoning.summary parameter for OpenAI models through the Responses API.
Linked regions now carry session transcripts, attachments and context across the regional recovery boundary.
Workflow change for replaying DynamoDB streams — Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing, enabling you to begin reading stream records from a specific point in time.
Local change for EKS ingress management — Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications.
Workflow change for Valkey diagnostics — Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now features ElastiCache Insights, a pre-built dashboard in Amazon CloudWatch for your node-based clusters.
Local change for IPv6 Spark jobs — Amazon EMR Serverless now supports IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity, expanding beyond the IPv4-only connectivity that was previously available.

Workflow change for testing location APIs — Amazon Location Service now offers a complete, interactive API Playground that lets developers explore and test every Places, Routes, and Maps API visually without writing code.
Local change for voice agent inference — Today, we announce the general availability of Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic, our latest speech-to-speech model for natural, real-time voice agents.
Local change for AWS console visualizations — Today, AWS announces enhanced visualization for Amazon Q Developer in the AWS Management Console.
Local change for regional table catalogs — Amazon S3 Tables now support up to 100 table buckets per AWS Region in an AWS account, increased from 10.

Workflow change for resizing workstation volumes — Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports the ModifyVolume API, which lets you change volume size, volume type, IOPS, or throughput in place, without detaching the volume or restarting the instance.

Local change for large Aurora clusters — Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs.
Local change for Trainium PyTorch development — Today, AWS launched the public beta of TorchNeuron, an open source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium.
Local change for EKS-backed batch authentication — AWS Batch now supports Amazon EKS access entry authentication for compute environments.
Workflow change for Brazilian license distribution — AWS Brazil now provides an automated distribution workflow through the AWS Brazil 2P Distribution Program.

Workflow change for remote client security — AWS Client VPN now supports device posture assessment, allowing you to verify that connecting user devices meet your security and compliance requirements before granting network access.

Workflow change for pipeline security testing — AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now integrates continuous penetration testing directly into your CI/CD pipeline (public preview) AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent) already provides continuous, on-demand penetration testing without the need to contract third-party pentest vendors.
Workflow change for RCS sender registration — Today, AWS End User Messaging adds a wizard that orchestrates the entire video capture for your RCS agent registration.
Local change for Iceberg maintenance — AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports table optimization, statistics, and crawlers for Apache Iceberg Version 3 (V3) tables.

Workflow change for Nextflow compute selection — Today, AWS HealthOmics introduces the resource fallback directive for tasks in your Nextflow workflows, enabling you to define an ordered list of preferred accelerator types, including an option to fallback to CPU instances.
Local change for identity store access — AWS IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience for your workforce to AWS accounts and applications.
Code listens directly on a port and serves HTTP frameworks without a Lambda request adapter.

Workflow change for private CA audits — AWS Private CA announces detailed certificate issuance logs, a new AWS CloudTrail service event that records the complete certificate content, issuing CA information, requester identity, and signing status for every issuance.

Local change for IAM metadata consumers — AWS is expanding programmatic service reference information to help you automate IAM policy management and keep your policies aligned with the latest service updates.
Workflow change for building migration networks — AWS Transform for migrations now gives you three ways to bring your network to AWS.

Workflow change for grounding model responses — Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now offers a Standard tier for contextual grounding checks, which detect and filter hallucinations by checking whether a model response is grounded in your reference source and relevant to the user's query.
The announcement describes eligibility, certification or guidance without documenting a change in customer workflow. Amazon Braket now in scope for FedRAMP Class C.
Local change for Canadian model inference — Amazon Bedrock now offers Canada cross-Region inference (CRIS) for Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5.
Local change for IPv6 VPC origins — Amazon CloudFront now supports end-to-end IPv6 delivery to origins inside your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), with the new dual-stack VPC origins.
Workflow change for contact center performance analysis — Amazon Connect Customer now scores the outcome of your customer interactions.
Local change for agent workspace layouts — Amazon Connect Customer now offers two different layouts that optimize screen space on the agent workspace.

Local change for OpenZFS transfers — AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for OpenZFS as a source or destination location, NFS version 4.2 for on-premises NFS servers and FSx for OpenZFS file systems, and a new ObjectMetadata option for object storage transfers.
Local change for AMI tag management — Amazon EC2 now supports AMI tag sharing, a new feature that lets AMI owners make selected tags visible to all AWS accounts an AMI is shared with.

Workflow change for ECS capacity consolidation — Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation.
Workflow change for updating existing cache durability — Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters.

Workflow change for organization-wide threat management — Amazon GuardDuty now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies, enabling you to centrally enable GuardDuty threat detection across every account and Region in your AWS organization.

Workflow change for migrating directory identity sources — AWS IAM Identity Center now retains your workforce identities and their assignments when you change your identity source from Active Directory to an external identity provider (IdP), such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, or to the Identity Center directory.

Workflow change for protecting recursive event flows — AWS Lambda recursive loop detection now automatically detects and stops recursive loops between Lambda Event Functions and Amazon EventBridge Custom event buses , helping protect you against unintended usage and unexpected charges from runaway workloads.

Workflow change for managing media connections — AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports managing connections through a new endpoint registry, which allows you to register devices or software external to MediaConnect and connect those endpoints to your router inputs and outputs.
Workflow change for firewall DNS validation — AWS Network Firewall now supports IP validation, extending domain-based filtering beyond HTTP/HTTPS to protocols such as SFTP and SSH.
Local change for latency-sensitive inference — Today, AWS announces the availability of Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock.

Local change for Oracle peering — Oracle Database@AWS (ODB) now supports advertising aggregate routes and a default route (0.0.0.0/0) when configuring ODB peering between applications in an Amazon VPC and databases in an ODB network.

Workflow change for governing agent actions — Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most.
Workflow change for Iceberg analytics — Amazon Redshift now supports the creation and refresh of Apache Iceberg materialized views.
Workflow change for DNS security monitoring — Route 53 Global Resolver and DNS Firewall now provide DNS analytics and insights through native Amazon CloudWatch integration.

Local change for custom Studio project tools — Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom Tooling blueprints, giving domain administrators the ability to define the foundation of every project by using their own AWS CloudFormation templates.
Local change for financial compliance audits — AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports automated security checks that align with the Cyber Risk Institute (CRI) profile.
Local change for IDC Studio preferences — Today, AWS announces light mode support in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for Identity Center (IDC) based domains.
Local change for serverless time-series analytics — Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.
Local change for managed SFTP logs — AWS Transfer Family now lets you choose a custom log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for managed workflow execution logs.
Local change for file transfer branding — The AWS Transfer Family console now supports SVG files for logos and ICO files for favicons in web apps, with upload limits increased to 2 MB.
Managed MCP service owns authentication and connection lifecycle in place of custom session handling.
Local change for schedule creation API clients — Amazon EventBridge Scheduler now has a higher default service quota for the CreateSchedule API action.
Local change for autoscaling DocumentDB clusters — Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) Serverless, an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration for DocumentDB, is now available on version 8.0.
Prefill and decode move to separate GPU pools connected through EFA and GPU-direct cache transfer.
Local change for large DocumentDB databases — Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) now supports a maximum storage limit of 256 TiB, doubling the previous limit of 128 TiB.
A single tunnel endpoint gives another account private reachability to a shared CIDR instead of separate per-resource configurations.
